chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: How the name Ink Spots came about
summary: At that time white theatres did not book Negroes, so little kids were billed as Ink Spots with three ink spots on the poster.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Just for the information of the person who's reading these

transcripts or whatever, we're going to go back a little bit in time again -- in fact to the beginning where it all started. You're talking about when you were very young, these songs you were singing when you were in your early 'teens?
When you first formed the ink spots, how old were you?
I don't quite understand how you came up with the name of Ink Spots.

Because that's what they give us at the theater. See, there weren't no negroes playing on the stage in that time in these white theaters and they wanted to put a name out there that everybody would kind of feel good about and they couldn't get people that had a big name to play that because they didn't have no negroes playing in that theater.

So they took like what we call little kids, you know, and they put the idea of the Ink Spots which would draw attraction, they'd take three spots of ink, understand,and put it on a piece of paper and you'd see the ink spots, that was the idea and they put Buck and Bubbles pictures on the thing, Buck and Sugar Babe and myself.
